concepts.title: Programming Languages for Biologists
concepts.definition: Biology now runs on code: PERL has handled bulk sequence data since bioinformatics began, Python - Guido van Rossum's 1991 object-oriented generalist - dominates sequence, structure and phylogenetic work on unix, mac and windows, R built by Robert Gentleman and Robert Ihaka supplies free statistical muscle, MATLAB rounds out analysis platforms, and newer designs like Microsoft's rule-based GEC and the Kera language with its Samhita biological library target living-cell engineering.
concepts.key_idea: Pick the language by the task - sequence crunching, statistics, visualisation or cell-system design - and most production work still sits on Linux.
question_patterns: which language sits at the core of sequence based large data handling since the beginning of bioinformatics
who created Python and in which year - list two reasons for its popularity among bioinformaticians
from which inventors does the R language take its name and what is it ideal for
what are the GEC and Kera languages designed for and what does the Samhita library hold
why should young biotechnology students learn basic programming and statistics
on which operating system platform have most successful bioinformatics applications been developed

solution_steps.explain: PERL for bulk sequences, Python for general analysis, R for statistics, MATLAB for platform analysis.
Python 1991 by van Rossum; R from Robert Gentleman and Robert Ihaka; GEC from Microsoft; Kera from Umesh P.
Linux hosts most successful applications; cloud and web servers extend reach.

worked_examples.q: Which language has handled bulk sequence data since bioinformatics began: PERL or COBOL?

concepts.title: Milestones in the Rise of Systems Biology
concepts.definition: The field grew in dated steps - Hodgkin and Huxley modelled the neuronal action potential in 1952, Denis Noble built the first computer model of the heart pacemaker in 1960, Mesarovic launched systems theory and biology in 1966, von Bertalanffy published the first theory in 1968, and the 2012 whole-cell model of Mycoplasma genitalium capped six decades of quantitative modelling.
concepts.key_idea: Subtract one milestone year from another to measure the field's growth spans.
question_patterns: how many years separate the Hodgkin-Huxley axon model from the Mycoplasma genitalium whole-cell model
who developed the first computer model of the heart pacemaker and when
at which 1966 venue was systems biology formally launched and by whom
why is von Bertalanffy's 1968 work called the precursor of the discipline
which institution built the 2012 whole-cell model and what can it predict
what challenge did the National Science Foundation pose and who joined MIT to answer it

solution_steps.explain: Span equals the later model year minus the earlier one.

worked_examples.q: Who modelled the neuronal action potential in 1952: Hodgkin and Huxley, or Noble?

concepts.title: Integration Theme versus Reductionism
concepts.definition: Reductionism catalogued the parts of living systems but stumbled at their pluralism; systems biology answers by integrating every component at once through network mapping joined to kinetics described with partial differential equations, letting quantitative models reveal emergent properties of cells, tissues and organisms.
concepts.key_idea: Parts alone explain little - map the network and bind its dynamics with mathematics to see the whole system behave.
question_patterns: why could reductionism not describe the pluralism of a biological system
what sits at the core of the theme of systems biology - state the mapping and equations involved
define systems biology as an interdisciplinary field with reference to life information and system science
give two examples of efficient system models used in systems biology
how did the human genome project seed the systems biology approach
which emergent properties can system models describe that single experiments miss

solution_steps.explain: Reductionism isolates components; systems biology integrates them simultaneously.
Object network mapping plus interdependent kinetics handled through partial differential equations.
Emergent functional properties become predictable in health and disease contexts.

worked_examples.q: Systems biology binds network dynamics with which mathematics: differential equations or arithmetic tables?

concepts.title: Protocol of a Systems Biology Experiment
concepts.definition: A systems biology study loops through a fixed protocol: define the problem, design and run the experiment, collect and format the data, build the network interface, transfer it into a mechanism-based model, compare simulation against experiment, fold every discrepancy back as a new hypothesis, and repeat until model and reality agree.
concepts.key_idea: Model, simulate, compare, revise - the cycle only converges when discrepancies become new hypotheses.
question_patterns: list the discrete steps of the workflow shown for implementing a systems biology experiment
why must the transferred network interface be precise and mechanism based
what happens to the discrepancies observed between simulation results and experimental data
which tasks does the computation workflow require besides data management
from where does deep curation draw literature pathways and database evidence
how does novel interaction network inference feed the proposed molecular map

solution_steps.explain: Problem definition precedes experiment design, execution and data collection.
Curated networks become a systems biology model whose dynamics are defined.
Simulation versus data discrepancies drive model updates and repeated testing.

worked_examples.q: In the systems biology protocol, what follows building the model: simulation or publication?

concepts.title: Data Management in Systems Biology
concepts.definition: Three pillars organise systems biology data: minimum information sets with their metadata for microarray, proteomic and biomedical studies; XML-style file formats that machines can process automatically; and ontologies such as Gene Ontology and Systems Biology Ontology that fix hierarchical meanings - all wired together by spreadsheets, electronic lab notebooks, LIMS and workflow engines like KNIME, Taverna and Galaxy.
concepts.key_idea: Report the minimum, encode in machine-readable formats, and let ontologies standardise what every term means.
question_patterns: name the three aspects considered for data management in systems biology
why are file formats in systems biology generally XML based
what do ontologies annotate and name two important examples
which workflow systems allow construction execution and sharing of specialised pipelines
match the facilities data management network inference simulation and docking with two tools each
what is the role of electronic lab notebooks and LIMS in modern laboratories

solution_steps.explain: Essential supporting information plus metadata accompanies every dataset.
XML-based formats allow automatic computer processing.
Ontologies supply hierarchical semantic annotation; workflow engines integrate the tools.

worked_examples.q: Which ontology fixes hierarchical meanings for gene terms: Gene Ontology or a dictionary?

concepts.title: Model Analysis Methods for Network Behaviour
concepts.definition: Built models are interrogated three ways: sensitivity analysis with tools like SBML-SAT probes stability and controllability against disturbances, bifurcation and phase-space analysis with AUTO or XPPAut uncovers steady and dynamical tendencies, and metabolic control analysis via MetNetMaker ties steady-state network properties back to individual reactions; the underlying partial differential equations are approximated numerically by the finite element method in ANSYS, FreeFEM++ or MATLAB.
concepts.key_idea: Stress the model, watch its states shift, and connect the network's steady state to its component reactions.
question_patterns: which three model analysis methods probe the behaviour of complex biological models
what do sensitivity analysis tools reveal about a system against distractions
what is the purpose of bifurcation and phase-space analysis
define metabolic control analysis and name its tool
what are PDEs and which numerical technique approximates their solutions
name two solvers used to solve the partial differential equations of spatiotemporal models

solution_steps.explain: Sensitivity analysis scores stability and controllability.
Bifurcation and phase-space work exposes steady and oscillatory tendencies.
Metabolic control analysis connects network-level properties to component reactions; FEM numerically solves the PDEs.

worked_examples.q: Which analysis probes a model's stability against disturbances: sensitivity analysis or titration?
